newsitem.title: UK: UK car industry worries over erratic sales, stg.
newsitem.headline: UK car industry worries over erratic sales, stg.

text.p: UK car industry leaders voiced concern on Tuesday about erratic retail sales levels in 1996 despite strong consumer spending in other parts of the UK economy and said that sterling strength posed a potential risk to export growth.

The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders outlined its concerns after announcing that 1996 car registrations rose 4.12 percent on 1995, with a monthly rise of 9.23 percent in December. But most of the annual growth was due to fleet car sales and heavy discounting which has eaten into manufacturers' margins.

The SMMT, the industry trade body, said that underneath some positive sales figures for 1996 -- which saw car registrations at their highest levels for seven years at 2.02 million -- there were worrying danger signs.
Margaret Pyne, head of economics at the SMMT, said "The erratic nature of retail demand was particularly disappointing."

On sterling's robust gains, Eric Thompson, SMMT chief executive, said "Obviously it's (sterling strength) a risk." The sales trend in the UK has shown imports take 62.03 percent of the UK market, up from 58.94 percent in 1995. In 1994, imports took just 52.82 percent of UK car sales.

Thompson warned that UK car makers would continue to feel the pressure with "intense competition and over-capacity hitting margins. Unless they start earning better profits it is difficult to see how they can afford to finance new models. That it a major concern throughout the world."

Industry analysts are even more cautious about prospects for 1997. Saying that any growth will come against a backdrop of margins being squeezed and UK car companies facing continued uncertainty from the strong pound.
European countries with weak home markets and currencies (versus stg) are also seen muscling further into the UK.

Arthur Maher, head of European forcasting at the motor industry analyst LMC International, told Reuters "With the French market in deep recession, their car makers' increased levels of aggression in the UK is a reflection of the state of the home market."
The UK also faces new entrants like South Korea's Daewoo.
On the potential damage to UK exports from stg, Maher said "In the short term, UK exports are likely to impact on company financials rather than sales volumes.
If sterling appreciation looks structural, manufacturers may look to reduce vehicle specifications and renew efforts to boost productivity."

While the SMMT says exports will continue to show pacy growth in 1997, analysts like Maher say that the industry cannot afford to be hit by an expensive pound abroad while the home retail market remains erratic and the fleet car market is artificially boosted by heavy discounting.
